1) the indirect immunoflorescence and complement fixation test results in chagasic renal transplant recipients did not show changes in the course of the infection; and 2) the indirect immunfluorescence test showed positive reactions in non-chagastic renal transplant recipients.

the immunosubpression state induced in renal transplantees did not promote exacerbation of the chagasic infection, and that the indirect immunoflorescence test for Chagases' disease is unsuitable for diagnosis in renal transplated patients.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the serologic diagnosis of Chagas's disease in patients submitted to renal transplants.
the serological diagnosis of Chagas disease, and the influence of the immunosuppressed state induced by immunosuppressive agents on the serological tests used for the diagnosis of the disease.
the study of the immunological mechanisms that may be involved in the pathogenesis of chronic chagasic cardiopathy.

the serological diagnosis of Chagas'disease in immunosupressed patients is not reliable, and the diagnosis must be based on clinical, epidemiological, and parasitological data, in addition to the serological results.
immunosuppressive therapy did not exacerbate chronic Chagas' disease or influence serological tests for diagnosis of the infection.
the immunosubpression state induced in chronic chagasic patients did not promote exacerbation of the Chagas' disease.
